newsitem.title: FRANCE: Troops kill 300 rebels in Algeria, newspapers say.
newsitem.headline: Troops kill 300 rebels in Algeria, newspapers say.

text.p: Troops backed by helicopters and bulldozers have killed more than 300 Moslem rebels and are besieging scores more in northeastern Algeria's mountains, Algerian newspapers said on Monday.

One newspaper quoted an army officer as warning civilians in villages, mainly south of Algiers, that Moslem guerrillas might stage more massacres and bomb attacks after rebel losses in a government offensive.
Hundreds of civilians have been killed in massacres and bomb attacks in towns and villages in the past two years when the country's strife took a more bloody turn.

More than 90 villagers, including women and childen, died in massacres last week in five attacks in hamlets in Blida province, about 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, and in the neighbouring Hadjout and Bou Smail areas.
Gunmen, thought to be Moslem guerrillas, on Sunday shot dead a leading doctor in the eastern town of Constantine, said Al Khabar newspaper.
Dr Ben Yahia, a member of the Rally for Culture and Democracy (RCD) led by anti-Islamist hawk Said Saadi, was shot five times in the head in his clinic, it said.

The military, in an offensive against Moslem rebels in areas which have been the focus of most killings in the past two years in Blida and Medea provinces, were besieging and shelling more rebel hideouts.
"More than 300 terrorists, including Emirs (gang leaders), have been killed by the security forces in a huge operation since July 14," said Le Matin newspaper.
The offensive focused on Attatba area in Blida region where other newspapers had put the number of guerrillas killed at up to 150.
Le Matin and Al Khabar said on Monday that troops had then moved to Sidi Bouzid, Magtaa Kheira and Oued el Alleug, south and west of Attatba, to encircle and pound scores more rebels holed up there.

"We encountered them here in this forest (in Magtaa Kheira)...The dogs wanted to flee into Oued el Alleug. They were firing and shouting 'Allahu Akbar' ('God is Greatest')," said Le Matin, quoting a government force member.
"We clashed with them all night and at dawn we put them under bombardment...," he added, talking about an unspecified number of rebels holed up in Magtaa Kheira.

Le Matin said security forces found 40 blockhouses in the area, each able to hold about 20 rebels. It said bulldozers guarded by soldiers began ploughing roads through the forest in the nearby Sidi Bouzid area.
"We will shell the area in the next few days," an army officer told Le Matin.

Al Khabar newspaper said about 50 rebels had taken refuge in Sidi Bouzid mountain. It said the operation in Attatba and neighbouring area was part of a large offensive across Moslem rebel strongholds.

"Troops, backed by paramilitary gendarmes and other security forces, are carrying out huge operations against terrorist hideouts in Chrea and Bougara in Blida, Zekkar in Ain Defla, 150 km (90 miles) south of Algiers, and Mougornou mountain in Medea province," the paper said.
The offensive coincided with candidate registration for multiparty local elections to be held on October 23.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria since 1992 when the authorities scrapped a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
